Session: `session_01PQ3NihCHE9LUtHoGxo6A9f`
Branch: `claude/issue-5458-unprefixed-query-options`
Worktree: `objectui-issue-5458`
Domain: `domain:devx` (@ objectui, seat #5748)
File surface: `eslint-rules/no-query-params-under-options.js` + its test; `apps/console/src/sdui-workbench-preview.tsx`; `packages/app-shell/src/views/ObjectView.tsx`; `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/AssignedUsersSection.tsx`. (stop on breach; explain in the report)
Container & model: `M`, `mode:subagent`, `model: opus` — the rule's scope is a judgement call. ⚠️ Tier is this seat's explicit decision; `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` does not exist in objectui.
Clause-②: no — **and the boundary is load-bearing here, so read the constraint below.** A lint rule that refuses more shapes tightens; it does not widen an acceptance set. What *would* be Clause-② is changing `convertQueryParams` to start honouring unprefixed keys, and that is forbidden below.
Serial constraints cleared: **PR #5925 is open against `packages/app-shell/`** — `src/preview/DraftChangesPanel.tsx`, comment-only, disjoint from the two `src/views/**` files here; read but ⛔ do not touch. Other open PRs by head: #5922 (layout docs), #5843 (governed `docs/adr`), #5774 (`.github/workflows/` + `ci-cd-pipeline.md`), #5400 (release), #4958 (dependabot) — none intersect. **Concurrent in this batch: #3840**, which touches `apps/console/src/__tests__/public-block-binding-reach.test.tsx` only — disjoint from your `apps/console` file, but ⛔ do not edit that probe.

## ⚠️ The census has changed since the card was written — 3 live sites, not 4

Re-measured on `origin/main` @ `2074a59`. The card's census was taken at `c40f3b8ca`, and **the fourth site is already fixed**. Use this table, ⛔ not the card's:

| site | card said | measured now |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `apps/console/src/sdui-workbench-preview.tsx` | `:65`, `find(…, { top: 200 })` | **live**, moved to **`:86`** |
| `packages/app-shell/src/views/ObjectView.tsx` | `:1561`, `find(…, { limit: 0 })` | **live**, moved to **`:1687`** |
| `.../metadata-admin/AssignedUsersSection.tsx` | `:109`, `find(…, { …, limit: 1 })` | **live**, still `:109` |
| `content/docs/guide/react-pages.md` | `:129`, `find(…, { filters: [[…]] })` | **ALREADY FIXED** — `:231` now reads `$filter: ['status', '=', 'open']`, and `:243` documents the rule in prose |

That doc page is now an **ally, not a target**: it already tells readers *"An unprefixed `filters:` or `top:` is not a query option"*. ⛔ Do not re-fix it, and do not count it in your before/after. Every line number above is a lead — re-derive from the tree, ⛔ do not trust mine either.

## Why this matters more than a lint nit

The failure is an **unbounded read**, not a truncated one. The platform's GET list route has no default page size, so a dropped cap returns the entire match set — invisible until the object is large. And `ObjectView.tsx`'s `limit: 0` inverts: `$top: 0` is honoured end-to-end as *no records*, so dropping the key turns "no rows" into "every row". Establish what that call is actually meant to do before you rewrite it — ⛔ a mechanical `limit` → `$top` there could be the wrong fix if the intent was never "no rows".

`AssignedUsersSection.tsx:109` sits one line from three correct calls (`$top: 500 / 200 / 1000`) — the shape a reviewer's eye slides over, which is the argument for the rule.

## ⛔ Hard constraint — fix the call sites, not the adapter

`QueryParams` declares only `$`-prefixed keys and `convertQueryParams` copies exactly those; the index signature is deliberate, because adapters legitimately take adapter-specific params. **⛔ Do not make the adapter start accepting unprefixed keys** — that widens the acceptance set, which is Clause-② work and a maintainer-floor decision, not this card's. If you conclude the adapter is the right place, **stop and report** rather than doing it.

## The rule — narrow on purpose

Extend `no-query-params-under-options` (or add a sibling; justify whichever you pick). The AST walk already lands on the params object of a `find`/`findOne` call, so this is a second predicate: flag a **static** key that is a known query-option name **missing its `$`** — `top`, `skip`, `filter`, `filters`, `select`, `orderby`, `sort`, `expand`, `search`, `count`, `limit`, `offset` — in the second argument. ⛔ **Not "any unprefixed key"** — that would flag the legitimate adapter-specific params the index signature exists for, and a rule that cries wolf gets disabled.

Requirements on the rule:

1. It must **fail on all three live sites before your fix** and pass after. Show both runs. A rule that only passes after the call sites are already fixed proves nothing about the rule.
2. It must **not** flag the correct neighbours (`$top: 500 / 200 / 1000` in the same file) — assert that explicitly, it is the false-positive control.
3. The existing sibling half (`{ options: { $top: 100 } }`) must keep failing. ⛔ No regression in what is already gated.
4. The rule must be **wired into the lint config that CI actually runs**. An unregistered rule file is a no-op that looks like a fix — verify by making it fire, not by reading config.

## One more thing the card noticed, and it is a real second defect

`sdui-workbench-preview.tsx` reads `all.records` off the result, but `find()` resolves to a `QueryResult` (`data`, never `records`) — so that preview lists nothing **regardless** of the cap. Fix it while you are in the file. ⚠️ `skills/objectui/guides/data-integration.md:268` publishes the same `return result.records;` to skill consumers — that is a **published skills surface**. ⛔ Do not edit `skills/**` on this card; if it is still wrong on today's tree, report it and I will file it, since published skill packages are evaluated whole-package and carry their own line budget.

## Premise-first

The body is a lead, not a specification. If a site is already fixed — one of four already was — report the measurement instead of manufacturing a diff. Read the card on GitHub yourself and **check the body for sanitizer truncation**; note it was moved verbatim from objectstack#10470, so bare refs there were rewritten.
